Alex (Sales): @Priya quick q from procurement — before we sign the POC we need to confirm what part of Redwood's environment is in scope for ISO-27001 evidence. Is it just the POC VPC or the whole tenant?
Maria (Security): Short answer: scope can be limited to the POC boundary if the customer contract and Statement of Applicability (SoA) call that out. We'll need an applicability statement from sales + the architecture diagram.
Priya (Customer): We prefer narrow scope (POC only). Procurement insists on clarity about key management and who holds keys. They want KMS details and rotation policy.
Maria (Security): For hosted Redwood API (shared), keys are managed by Redwood KMS for tenant encryption at rest; we provide key usage descriptions and key rotation cadence. For Dedicated/Private, customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own) is supported — that changes evidence ownership.
Devon (Solutions Eng): POC architecture: we'll provision an isolated Dedicated pool in customer region (if they want isolated capacity) or a VPC peered Private deployment. Either way, we can use customer KMS via AWS KMS/EKS or HSM integration.
Alex (Sales): Procurement also asked for a mapping to SIG/CAIQ controls for our hosting setup — they sent a questionnaire. Can we give a short mapping and sample artifacts?
Maria (Security): Yes — we have a SIG/CAIQ mapping sheet and an ISO SoA extract. I'll attach a sanitized evidence bundle (policies, encryption config screenshots, rotation logs) to the RFP. Note: some artifacts reference tenant-level controls which only apply for full-tenant ISO; we'll mark those as N/A for POC scope.
Priya (Customer): Timeline? They want evidence within 3 business days to keep the POC kickoff.
Maria (Security): I can assemble a POC-focused package:
- SoA snippet indicating scoped controls
- Architecture diagram with boundary clearly highlighted
- KMS usage statement (who holds keys, rotation interval, CMKs vs data keys)
- Sample audit logs and last rotation date (redacted)
I'll need confirmed POC architecture (Dedicated vs Hosted) and contact for a redaction review.
Devon (Solutions Eng): If we go Dedicated, I can export the KMS policy and IAM role bindings. If Hosted, I'll include our tenant KMS statement and token isolation notes. Also note: for streaming and KV cache we use ephemeral encryption keys per request in addition to disk encryption.
Alex (Sales): I'll confirm with the buyer and share the architecture choice. One more ask from procurement: will Redwood accept an appendix limiting ISO acceptance to the POC env?
Maria (Security): We can accept an appendix limiting acceptance to the scoped env. Legal and Compliance will need to sign a tailored applicability statement. That will explicitly list excluded controls.
Priya (Customer): Great. Also they asked about evidence retention window for logs — 90 days is fine?
Maria (Security): For POC we typically provide 90 days of relevant logs/screenshots. For enterprise contracts we can negotiate longer retention as an add-on.
InfraBot: Automated note: evidence bundle template created by @Maria (Security) at 1769456920. Reference: rdb-evidence/poc-templates/iso.
Alex (Sales): Perfect — I'll get the buyer to pick Dedicated vs Hosted today and send the PO. Maria, can you target sending the bundle within 48 hours once I confirm?
Maria (Security): Yes — aiming for <48 hours once architecture is confirmed. I'll also include a short SIG/CAIQ mapping PDF highlighting differences for POC scope.
Priya (Customer): Thanks all — procurement will expect a redaction window for screenshots before we share externally.
Maria (Security): Understood — we'll send docs to you first for redaction review.
Alex (Sales): Closing loop: next steps for me: confirm architecture w/ buyer, request redaction contact, and upload to the RFP thread. Will follow up here when done. :thumbsup:
Priya (Customer): Thanks!
Maria (Security): Thanks team.
__note: This file represents a single Slack thread. Messages are chronological and prefixed with sender names per agents.md.
